αἰακίδαο: Αἰακίδης — son or descendant of Aeacus, used of Achilles; masc. gen. sg., epic -αο (= Attic -ου)
αἳ: ὅς, ἥ, ὅ — who, which; relative pron., fem. nom. pl. · also demonstrative ὁ, ἡ, τό (in Homer a pronoun), fem. nom. pl.: ’they’; αἳ μέν … αἳ δέ ’some … others’ · also fem. nom. pl. with a dual verb (a dual subject, two goddesses): ’the two’
αἴ: εἰ — if; conditional conj., epic/dialectal by-form αἰ (used before κε)
αἴας: Αἴας — Ajax, Greek hero at Troy; masc. nom. sg.
αὐτοῖο: αὐτός — self; masc. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic αὐτοῦ): ’him’, after πάροιθε ’before him’
αὐτὰρ: αὐτάρ — but, and then; epic conj. (= Attic δέ, ἀλλά)
αὐτὸς: αὐτός — self; masc. nom. sg., intensive with the subject: ’myself, yourself, himself’
αὐτῇ: αὐτός — self; intensive pron., fem. dat. sg., agreeing with a dative: ’to her herself’ (αὐτῇ περ νοεούσῃ ’even though she herself understands’) · also fem. dat. sg. as a plain pronoun after ἅμα: ’with her’
αὔτως: αὔτως — just so, idly, without more; adv.: ’merely, to no purpose’
βάτην: βαίνω — go, walk; aor. 3 dual, unaugmented (= Attic ἐβήτην): ’the two went’
βρισῆος: Βρισεύς — Briseus, father of Briseis; masc. gen. sg., epic -ῆος (= Attic -έως)
γένοιτο: γίγνομαι — become, come to be; aor. opt. 3 sg., in a condition after εἰ: ’should become’ · also in a wish after αἲ γάρ: ’would that it might come to be’ · also in a purpose clause after ἵνα: ’might become’ · also in a main clause with κε, potential: ’would come to be, would be left’
γέρον: γέρων — old man; masc. voc. sg.: ’old man!’
γε: γε — at least, in fact, indeed; limiting/emphatic particle
γενεῇ: γενεή — birth, lineage, descent; fem. dat. sg.: ’by birth’
γερήνιος: Γερήνιος — Gerenian, standing epithet of Nestor; masc. nom. sg.; meaning uncertain — perhaps from a place Gerenia, or linked to γέρας ’honour’
γυναικῶν: γυνή — woman; fem. gen. pl., partitive after δῖα: ’the divine one among women’ · also fem. gen. pl., dependent on χερσί: ’of the women’ · also fem. gen. pl. after πρό: ’in defence of the wives’ (πρὸ γυναικῶν ’in front of, for their wives’)
γυναῖκας: γυνή — woman, wife; fem. acc. pl.
δ: δέ (elided δ’) — and, but · also the elided suffix -δε, ’to, toward’ (Ἄργος δ’ ’to Argos’)
δέ: δέ — and, but; connective particle · also the enclitic suffix -δε, ’to, toward’ (Οὔλυμπον δέ ’to Olympus’)
δέγμενος: δέχομαι — receive; wait for, await; syncopated aor. part. mid. masc. nom. sg. with present sense, epic (= Attic δεξάμενος)
δέπας: δέπας — cup, drinking-cup; neut. acc. sg. (nom. identical)
δεπάεσσιν: δέπας — cup; neut. dat. pl., epic -εσσιν (= Attic δέπασι)
διὶ: Ζεύς — Zeus, chief of the gods; masc. dat. sg. Διί
διῒ: Ζεύς — Zeus; dat. sg., epic Διΐ (= Διί); Διῒ φίλος ’dear to Zeus’
δώσω: δίδωμι — give; fut. 1 sg.: ’I will give’
δὲ: δέ — and, but; connective particle · also the enclitic suffix -δε, ’to, toward’ (οἶκον δὲ ’homeward’)
δὴ: δή — indeed, now, in fact; emphatic particle
δῖος: δῖος — heavenly, divine, illustrious; masc. nom. sg., epithet of heroes (= fem. δῖα)
δῶρ: δῶρον — gift; neut. acc. pl., elided (δῶρ’ = δῶρα) · also neut. nom. pl., elided: ’gifts’ (δῶρ’ Ἀφροδίτης ’the gifts of Aphrodite’)
εἰ: εἰ — if; conditional conj. · also ’whether’, introducing an indirect question · εἰ δή ’if indeed, since’ · also εἰ δ’ ἄγε ’come now’, a hortatory idiom
εἰμι: εἰμί — be; pres. 1 sg., enclitic (accent goes to the word before): ’I am’
εἴη: εἰμί — be; pres. opt. 3 sg.: ’it might be, he might be’; potential with κεν: ’it would be’ · also in a wish after εἴθε: ’would that it were’
εἷσεν: ἵζω — seat, set; aor. 3 sg. transitive: ’seated, set’
εὐπήκτῳ: εὔπηκτος — well-framed, well-fastened (εὖ + πήγνυμι); adj., neut. dat. sg., agreeing with μεγάρῳ
εὐρυβάτης: Εὐρυβάτης — Eurybates, Odysseus’ herald (’wide-strider’); masc. nom. sg.
εὔχομαι: εὔχομαι — declare oneself, avow, boast, pray; pres. 1 sg., + inf.: ’I declare myself (to be)’
εὗρον: εὑρίσκω — find; aor. 3 pl. act. (augmented εὗρον = Attic ηὗρον)
ζεὺς: Ζεύς — Zeus, king of the gods; nom. sg.
ζυγὸν: ζυγόν — yoke; neut. acc. sg., after ὑπό in tmesis with ἤγαγεν: ’under the yoke’ · also neut. acc. sg., after ὑπέρ: ’over the yoke’ (ὑπὲρ ζυγόν)
θ: τε (elided and aspirated θ’ before a rough breathing) — and; connective particle
θέμις: θέμις — custom, what is right, established usage; fem. nom. sg.
θέμιστας: θέμις — custom, established right, ordinance; fem. acc. pl.: ’ordinances, customary rights’
θεοὶ: θεός — god; nom. pl. · also voc. pl. (same form): ’you gods!’
θεὸν: θεός — god; masc. acc. sg. · also fem. acc. sg. of a goddess (θεός is common gender): ’goddess’ (δεινὴν … θεόν ’a fearsome goddess’)
θυμός: θυμός — life, the life-breath that leaves the body; also heart, spirit; masc. nom. sg.
θυμὸν: θυμός — heart, spirit, soul; acc. sg. · also the life that leaves the body: ’life’ (θυμὸν ὀλέσσῃ ’lose his life’)
θύγατρες: θυγάτηρ — daughter; fem. nom. pl., epic (= Attic θυγατέρες)
θῖνα: θίς — shore, beach; fem. acc. sg.
κ: κε(ν) (elided κ’) — epic particle marking a conditioned or potential action (= Attic ἄν)
κέ: κε(ν) — epic particle (= Attic ἄν); accented before an enclitic · with αἴ + subj.: ’if perhaps’ · with a relative + fut. indic.: ’who will, in that event’ · also εἰς ὅ κέ + fut. or short-vowel subj.: ’until’ (εἰς ὅ κέ σ’ … ποιήσεται ’until he makes you’) · also + fut. indic. in a main clause: ’will’ (καί κέ τις … ἐρέει ’someone will say’) · also ὄφρά κέ + subj.: ’until’ (… κέ … ἐνείκω ’until I bring’) · also ὥς κέ + opt., in a wish: ’so … might’ · also with an aor. indic., contrary to fact: ’would have’ (ἔνθά κέ τοι … φάνη ’there would have appeared to you’) · also + opt., potential: ’would’ (οὐδέ κέ τίς … ἀτιμήσειε ’no one would dishonour’)
κέν: κε(ν) — epic particle marking a conditioned or potential action (= Attic ἄν); accented before an enclitic
καλῇ: καλός — beautiful, fair, fine; fem. dat. sg.
κε: κε(ν) — epic particle marking a conditioned or potential action (= Attic ἄν); with the subj. in purpose and general clauses · also + subj. in a temporal or conditional clause: ’whenever’, ’if’ · also + fut. indic. in a main clause: ’shall’ (κε μελήσεται ’will concern’) · also + opt., potential: ’would’ (τώ κε … ἠμύσειε ’then would collapse’) · also with an impf. indic., past potential: ’would have’ (κε … ἔπασχον ’I would have suffered’) · also with an aor. indic., past potential: ’would have’ (κε σήκασθεν ’would have been penned’) · also + opt. in a condition after εἰ: ’if … might’ · also εἰς ὅ κε + aor. subj.: ’until’ (εἰς ὅ κε … εὕρωμεν ’until we find’)
κεν: κε(ν) — epic particle (= Attic ἄν); with the opt., potential: ’might, would’; with the subj. in conditions after εἰ, αἰ · also + subj. or fut. indic. in a main or relative clause: ’shall’ (’I shall take’; ’to whom I come’) · also + subj. in a general relative clause: ’whatever’ (ὅττί κεν εἴπῃς) · also with a past indic., contrary to fact: ’would have’ (ἔνθά κεν … ἐτύχθη) · also with an impf. indic., past potential: ’would be’ (κεν … κέρδιον ἦεν ’it would be better’) · also + subj. in a temporal clause after εἰς ὅ: ’until’ (εἰς ὅ κεν … μάχωνται ’until they fight’) · also εἴ κεν + opt., in a condition: ’if … should’ · also + subj. in a purpose clause after ὥς: ’so that … may’ · also + subj. in a temporal clause after ὅτε: ’whenever’ (ὅτε κεν … ἵκωμαι ’whenever I come’)
κλισίας: κλισίη — hut, shelter (of soldiers); fem. acc. pl., Ionic (= Attic κλισίας from κλισία)
κλισίην: κλισίη — hut, shelter, tent; fem. acc. sg. (Attic κλισία)
κλισίης: κλισίη — hut, shelter; fem. gen. sg., Ionic -ης (= Attic κλισίας), with ἐκ: ’out of the hut’
κλισμοῖσι: κλισμός — reclining chair, seat; masc. dat. pl., epic -οισι (= Attic -οις)
κούρη: κούρη — girl, maiden; fem. nom. sg. (ἠΰτε κούρη ’like a girl’) · also ’daughter’ (κούρη Διός ’daughter of Zeus’)
κοῦροι: κοῦρος — young man, boy; masc. nom. pl. · also masc. voc. pl., in address: ’youths!’ (κοῦροι Ἀχαιῶν ’youths of the Achaeans’)
κρητῆρα: κρητήρ — mixing-bowl (for wine and water); masc. acc. sg.
κρητῆρας: κρητήρ — mixing-bowl (for wine and water); masc. acc. pl.
κύδιστε: κύδιστος — most glorious, greatest; masc. voc. sg., superlative, address
κῆρι: κῆρ — heart; neut. dat. sg., epic (= Attic καρδίᾳ), in the idiom περὶ κῆρι ’exceedingly, at heart’ (περί an adverb)
λαὸν: λαός — people, host; masc. acc. sg.
λαῶν: λαός — people, host; masc. gen. pl.: ’of the people’
λιπὼν: λείπω — leave, leave behind; aor. part. act. masc. nom. sg.: ’having left’
μάλ: μάλα (elided μάλ’) — very, very much, by all means; adv.
μάλα: μάλα — very, very much, exceedingly; adv.
μάλιστα: μάλα — very, much; superl. adv. μάλιστα: ’most of all, especially’ · also ’for the most part, mostly’ (μάλιστα ἦμαρ ’the greater part of the day’)
μέγα: μέγας — great, huge; neut. nom./acc. sg. · also neut. acc. sg. used adverbially: ’greatly’ (μέγα νήπιοι ’greatly foolish’)
μέγαν: μέγας — great, big; masc. acc. sg.
μέγας: μέγας — great, big; masc. nom. sg.
μέν: μέν — on the one hand; truly; particle, often answered by δέ; acute before an enclitic; ἦ μέν ’truly’ in oaths · also asseverative, = μήν ’surely, truly’ (οὐ μέν πως ’surely not in any way’)
μή: μή — not; the negative of wish, command, fear and condition (where οὐ is the negative of fact) · also ’lest’, with the subj. · also ’lest’ with the opt. (μή … δευοίατο ’lest they lack’) · also ’lest’ with a dual verb in -ετον: ’lest the two … hang back’
μείζονα: μείζων — greater, larger; comparative of μέγας; masc. acc. sg., agreeing with λᾶαν
μεγάρῳ: μέγαρον — hall, great room; neut. dat. sg.
μετ: μετά (elided μετ’) — among, after; + acc.: ’to, among’ (motion) · also + dat.: ’among’ (μετ’ ἀθανάτοισιν) · also + acc., ’next after’ (μετ’ ἀμύμονα Πηλεΐωνα) · also + acc., ’after, in pursuit of’
μετὰ: μετά — among, with, after; + dat./acc./gen. · also an adverb, ’among them’, or a preverb in tmesis · also + acc. in μετὰ νῶτα βαλών: ’behind, with the back turned’
μιν: μιν — him, her, it; epic encl. acc. pron. (= Attic αὐτόν/αὐτήν/αὐτό)
μοί: ἐγώ — I; dat. sg., accented μοί before the enclitic that follows: ’to me, for me’
μοι: ἐγώ — I; encl. dat. sg.: ’to me, for me’ · also dat. of possession or interest: ’my’ (μοι ἵπποι ’my horses’)
μυρμιδόνων: Μυρμιδόνες — the Myrmidons, Achilles’ people; masc. gen. pl.
μὲν: μέν — on the one hand; particle, often answered by δέ · also asseverative, = μήν ’truly, indeed’: οὐ μὲν δή ’surely not’
μῦθον: μῦθος — word, speech, thing said; acc. sg. · also a plan, scheme agreed on (τοῖον...τελέωμεν μῦθον ’let us carry out this plan’) · also a pledge, promise (τὸν μῦθον ὑπέστημεν ’the promise we undertook’)
νέστωρ: Νέστωρ — Nestor, king of Pylos; masc. nom. sg.
νυ: νυ — now, then; weak enclitic particle (= νῦν, Attic νυν)
νώμησαν: νωμάω — deal out, distribute, wield; aor. 3 pl., unaugmented (= Attic ἐνώμησαν)
νῆα: ναῦς — ship; fem. acc. sg., epic νῆα
νῆας: ναῦς — ship; fem. acc. pl., epic νῆας (= Attic ναῦς)
οἱ: οἱ — encl. dat. sg. pron. ’to/for him, her’ · also ὁ, ἡ, τό, masc. nom. pl. ’they’ · also masc. nom. pl. with a noun, article-like: ’the’ (οἱ ἄριστοι ’the best men’)
οἳ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it (in Homer a pronoun); masc. nom. pl., ’they’ · also relative ὅς, masc. nom. pl., ’who’
οἵ: ὅς, ἥ, ὅ — who, which; relative pron., masc. nom. pl. · also demonstrative, with γε: ’they’ (οἵ γ’ ἀθέριζον) · also encl. dat. sg. οἱ, accented before a following enclitic: ’to him’ (δέ οἵ ἐστ’ ’and his … is’)
οἶκον: οἶκος — house, household; masc. acc. sg., with the suffix -δε: οἶκον δέ ’homeward, to his house’ · also masc. acc. sg. without -δε, after κατά: ’in the house, at home’ · also masc. acc. sg. without -δε, goal after εἰς: ’into the house’
οἶος: οἶος — alone, only; masc. nom. sg.
οὐδ: οὐδέ (elided οὐδ’) — and not, nor, not even
οὐδέ: οὐδέ — and not, nor, not even; neg. conj.
οὐκέτ: οὐκέτι — no longer; adv., elided (οὐκέτ’ = οὐκέτι)
οὔ: οὐ — not; neg. adv., in a question expecting the answer ’yes’ · also the plain negative adverb in a declarative statement, with no question implied: ’not’
πάντα: πᾶς — all, every; neut. acc. pl.: ’all (things)’ · also masc. acc. sg., agreeing with a name: ’all (through the whole of)’ (Αἰγιαλόν τ’ ἀνὰ πάντα) · also neut. acc. pl. adverbially: ’in every respect, in all things’ · also neut. nom. pl., agreeing with ταῦτα: ’all’ (ταῦτα … πάντα ’all these things’)
πάντεσσι: πᾶς — all, every; masc. dat. pl., epic -εσσι (= Attic πᾶσι)
πάτροκλος: Πάτροκλος — Patroclus, Achilles’ closest companion; masc. nom. sg.
πέλει: πέλω — be, come to be; pres. 3 sg., epic (= Attic ἐστί): ’is, exists’
πήδασον: Πήδασος — Pedasus, a Trojan, son of Bucolion; masc. acc. sg. · also Pedasus, a town on the Satnioeis; fem. acc. sg.
παρέσσεται: πάρειμι — be at hand, be present; fut. 3 sg., epic doubled σ (= Attic παρέσται): ’will be at hand’
παρὰ: παρά — beside, along, from; + dat./acc./gen. · also adv., ’beside (him)’ (παρὰ δὲ … Ἥρη ’and beside him Hera’)
πειρᾶν: πειράω — try, test; pres. inf. act., used as a command: ’try!’
περ: περ — even, though; enclitic particle, concessive or intensive; εἴ περ ’even if’
περικλυτὰ: περικλυτός — very famous, renowned; neut. acc. pl., agreeing with ἔργα · also neut. acc. pl., agreeing with δῶρα: ’very famous (gifts)’
πηλεΐωνα: Πηλεΐων — son of Peleus, i.e. Achilles; masc. acc. sg., patronymic
πηληϊάδεω: Πηληϊάδης — son of Peleus, i.e. Achilles; masc. gen. sg., epic -εω (= Attic -ου)
πηλῆος: Πηλεύς — Peleus, father of Achilles; masc. gen. sg., epic -ῆος (= Attic -έως)
πιθήσας: πιθέω (epic aor. ἐπίθησα; cf. πείθομαι) — trust, obey (+ dat.); aor. part. act. masc. nom. sg.: ’obeying’
πολλὰ: πολύς — much, many; neut. acc. pl.; also adverbial, ’much, earnestly’ · also neut. nom. pl., agreeing with ἔργα: ’many (works)’
πολλῇ: πολύς — much, many, great; fem. dat. sg.: ’thick, great’
πολλῶν: πολύς — much, many; gen. pl., of persons: ’of many (men)’
πολυφλοίσβοιο: πολύφλοισβος — loud-roaring; adj., fem. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -ου)
ποσσὶν: πούς — foot; masc. dat. pl., epic double σ (= Attic ποσί)
ποτε: ποτέ — once, at some time, ever; enclitic adv. · with a negative or ἤν: ’never, if ever’
ποτοῖο: πότος — drink, drinking; masc. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -ου), of what fills: ’with drink’
πριάμοιο: Πρίαμος — Priam, king of Troy; masc. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -ου)
προγενέστερος: προγενής — born before, elder; adj., comparative προγενέστερος, masc. nom. sg.: ’older’
προσέειπεν: προσεῖπον — speak to, address; aor. 3 sg., epic uncontracted, augment ἐ- kept (= Attic προσεῖπε)
προσέφη: πρόσφημι — speak to, address; aor. 3 sg.
προτέρω: πρότερος — before, further; comp. adv. προτέρω: ’farther on’
πρόσθ: πρόσθε — before, in front of; prep. + gen., elided πρόσθ’ (= πρόσθε): ’before (the others)’
πρώτιστα: πρώτιστος — first of all (epic double superlative of πρῶτος); neut. acc. pl. used adverbially: ’first of all’
πρὸς: πρός — towards, to; prep. + acc. · also + gen.: ’from, at the hands of’ (πρὸς Τρώων ’from the Trojans’) · also + gen. of witnesses: ’before, in the sight of’ (πρὸς θεῶν ’before the gods’) · also preverb in tmesis, apart from its verb (πρὸς … ἔειπεν ’addressed’) · also adv., ’besides’ (πρὸς δ’ … ῥῆξε ’and besides … broke’) · also prep. + dat.: ’on, against’ (πρὸς χρυσῇ περόνῃ ’on a golden brooch’)
πόδας: πούς — foot; acc. pl., accusative of respect · also acc. pl., direct object: ’feet’ (πόδας καὶ χεῖρας ’feet and hands’)
πόλλ: πολύς — much, many; neut. acc. pl., elided (πόλλ’ = πολλά): ’many’ · also neut. acc. pl. adverbially: ’much, greatly’ (πόλλ’ ἀεκαζομένη ’much against her will’)
πύλου: Πύλος — Pylos, city in the Peloponnese, home of Nestor; fem. gen. sg.
πώ: πώ — yet, up to now; enclitic adv. (usually with a negative)
πᾶσαι: πᾶς — all, every; fem. nom. pl., with πύλαι · also fem. nom. pl. with another fem. noun: ’all’ (πᾶσαι χολάδες ’all the bowels’) · also fem. nom. pl., in apposition to a pronoun: ’all (of them)’ (αἳ … πᾶσαι ’they all’)
πᾶσιν: πᾶς — all, every; masc./neut. dat. pl. (ν-movable)
σιωπῇ: σιωπή — silence; fem. dat. sg., dative of manner: ’in silence’
σκήπτρῳ: σκῆπτρον — staff, sceptre; neut. dat. sg.
σὺν: σύν — with, together with; prep. + dat. · also preverb in tmesis, apart from its verb (σὺν … ταράξῃ = συνταράξῃ ’throw into confusion’)
τ: τε (elided τ’) — and; ’epic τε’ also marks a general truth; in τ’ ἄρ with a question, ’then’ · also epic τε attached to ἦ, strengthening it: ἦ τ’ ’truly indeed’
τάλαντα: τάλαντον — scales, balance (also a weight, a talent); neut. acc. pl., the plural for a pair of scales
τάχιστα: ταχύς — quick, swift; superl. neut. acc. pl. as adv. τάχιστα: ’most quickly’
τάων: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun); fem. gen. pl., epic (= Attic τῶν): partitive, ’of these’ · also governed by πρόσθ’: ’before these’ · also fem. gen. pl., antecedent of a relative: ’of those’ (τάων ἃς … ’of those which …’) · also relative, fem. gen. pl.: ’whose’ (τάων ἐν κονίῃσι ’in whose dust’)
ταῦτά: οὗτος, αὕτη, τοῦτο — this; neut. nom./acc. pl.: ’these things’, accented before an enclitic · also elided ταῦτ’
ταῦτα: οὗτος, αὕτη, τοῦτο — this; neut. nom./acc. pl.: ’these things’
τε: τε — and, both...and; enclitic connective; also ’epic τε’ marking a standing general truth in relative clauses
τι: τις, τι — someone, something; neut. nom./acc. sg. · in ὅ τι, ’whatever, why’ (= ὅτι) · also adverbial acc. with οὐ: ’at all’ (οὔ τι δυνήσεαι ’you will not at all be able’) · also adverbial acc. after εἰ: ’at all’ (εἴ ποτε δή τι … ὤνησας ’if ever you helped at all’) · also neut. acc. sg. with κακόν after μή: ’some’ (μή τι … ῥέξῃ κακὸν ’lest he do some evil’) · also adverbial acc. after μή: ’at all’ (μή τι διατρίβειν ’not to delay at all’) · also neut. acc. sg., object of πάσχω after μή: ’any (harm)’ (μή τι πάθοι ’lest he suffer any harm’) · also adverbial acc. after αἴ κεν: ’somehow’ (αἴ κέν τι … γένηαι ’if somehow you become’) · also adverbial acc. after οὐδέ, with a partitive gen.: ’at all’ (οὐδέ τι τῶν μέμνηται ’nor does he remember any of it’)
τις: τις, τι — someone, something, a certain one; indefinite pron., masc./fem. nom. sg. · also with a negative: ’any, anyone’ (οὐ … τις ’no one’; οὐδέ τις ’nor any’) · also after the relative ὅς, indefinite: ὅς τις ’whichever, whoever’ · also after ὅς, as an indirect interrogative: ὅς τις ὅδ’ ἐστίν ’who this is’ · also after εἰ: ’if anyone’ (εἴ τις …) · also after μή: ’lest any’ (μή τις Δαναῶν ’lest any of the Danaans’)
τοι: σύ — you (sg.); encl. dat. sg.: ’to/for you’ · also τοι, the affirming particle: ’you know, indeed’ (esp. in ἦ τοι, οὔ τοι); the two are not always easy to keep apart
τοὔνεκα: τοὔνεκα (crasis of τοῦ ἕνεκα) — for this reason, therefore; adv.
τοὺς: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc. acc. pl. ’them’ · also relative, masc. acc. pl.: ’whom’ · also masc. acc. pl. with a noun, article-like: ’the’ (τοὺς ἄλλους ’the others’)
τοῖσι: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc. dat. pl. ’to/among them’
τοῦτον: οὗτος, αὕτη, τοῦτο — this; masc. acc. sg.: ’this man’
τρεῖς: τρεῖς — three; numeral, masc./fem. nom. pl. · also masc./fem. acc. pl. (same form)
τόσσα: τόσος — so much, so many; epic τόσσος (doubled σ), neut. acc. pl.
τότ: τότε — then, at that time; adv., elided (τότ’ = τότε)
τὰς: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); fem. acc. pl. as a relative, ’which’ (τὰς Εὔμηλος ἔλαυνε ’which Eumelus drove’) · also fem. acc. pl. demonstrative: ’these, them’ (τὰς διαπέρσαι ’to sack these’)
τὴν: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); fem. acc. sg.: ’her’ · also relative, fem. acc. sg.: ’which’ (τὴν πρῶτον ἐπηπείλησ’ ’which he first threatened’) · also fem. acc. sg. with a noun, demonstrative: ’that’ (τὴν ὁδόν ’that journey’)
τὸν: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc. acc. sg., ’him’; with a noun, ’that’ · also relative, ’whom’
τὼ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it (in Homer a pronoun); dual nom.: ’the two of them, those two’ · also dual acc.: ’those two’ (τὼ γὰρ νεικείεσκε) · also τὼ = τῷ, adv.: ’therefore, so’ (τὼ οὐκ ἂν … ἀγορεύοις) · also dual relative: ’whom’
τῆς: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun); fem. gen. sg. · also fem. gen. sg. with the force of a relative: ’of which’ · also fem. gen. sg. ’for her’, gen. of cause after ἀχέων (τῆς … ἀχέων ’grieving for her’)
τῇ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; fem. dat. sg. · with an ordinal, ’on the (day)’: τῇ δεκάτῃ ’on the tenth’ · also adverbial, ’by that way, there’ · also fem. dat. sg. as relative adverb: ’by which way’ (τῇ … ἔμελλε διεξίμεναι ’by which he was about to go out’)
φάτο: φημί — say, speak; impf. 3 sg. mid., unaugmented (= ἔφατο)
φίλην: φίλος — dear, one’s own; fem. acc. sg.
φίλοι: φίλος — dear, friendly; masc. voc. pl. (identical with nom.), in address: ’friends!’ · also masc. nom. pl., predicate: ’dear, welcome’ (μῦθοι φίλοι)
φίλος: φίλος — dear, beloved; masc. nom. sg., predicate: ’dear (to him)’ · also attributive, ’dear’ (φίλος υἱός ’dear son’) · also masc. voc. sg., in address: ’dear (Menelaus)’
φρένα: φρήν — mind, wits, heart; fem. acc. sg.
φρένας: φρήν — mind, heart, wits (lit. midriff); fem. acc. pl.
φρεσὶ: φρήν — mind, heart, wits; fem. dat. pl.
φωνήσας: φωνέω — utter, raise one’s voice; aor. part. masc. nom. sg.: ’having raised his voice’
φῦλα: φῦλον — tribe, race; neut. nom./acc. pl.: ’tribes’
φῶτας: φώς — man, warrior, mortal; masc. acc. pl.
χαλκοῦ: χαλκός — bronze, copper; masc. gen. sg.: πλεῖαι χαλκοῦ ’full of bronze’
χόλοιο: χόλος — anger, bile; masc. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -ου), after λῆγε (ceasing from)
ψεῦδος: ψεῦδος — falsehood, lie; neut. nom. sg., predicate: ’a falsehood’
ἀΐδης: Ἀΐδης — Hades, god of the dead; masc. nom. sg., epic (= Attic Ἅιδης)
ἀγέσθω: ἄγω — lead; mid. lead for oneself, take home; pres. imper. 3 sg. mid.: ’let him lead (home)’
ἀγαμέμνων: Ἀγαμέμνων — Agamemnon, king of Mycenae, leader of the Achaeans at Troy; masc. nom. sg.
ἀλλ: ἀλλά (elided ἀλλ’) — but; well then · also ’except’: ’but only’ (ἀλλ’ οἶοι ’except us two’)
ἀμπελόεσσαν: ἀμπελόεις — rich in vines, vine-clad; fem. acc. sg., agreeing with Φρυγίην
ἀμύμονα: ἀμύμων — blameless, excellent (traditional sense; exact meaning uncertain); adj. of two endings, acc. sg. (masc./fem.) · also neut. nom./acc. pl.
ἀνέστη: ἀνίστημι — stand up, rise; aor. 3 sg. intrans.: ’stood up’
ἀνθρώπων: ἄνθρωπος — human being, man; masc. gen. pl.
ἀντί: ἀντίος — facing, opposite; neut. acc. pl. ἀντία used as adv. + gen., elided (ἀντί’ = ἀντία): ’opposite, facing’
ἀπερείσι: ἀπερείσιος — boundless, unstinted; neut. acc. pl., elided (ἀπερείσι’ = ἀπερείσια)
ἀπηύρων: ἀπαυράω — take away, deprive of; impf. 3 pl., epic (augmented ἀπ-ηύρων), + acc. of the thing taken: ’they took away’
ἀργείην: Ἀργεῖος — Argive, of Argos; adj., fem. acc. sg., epic -είην (= Attic Ἀργείαν)
ἀρούρης: ἄρουρα — ploughed land, field; fem. gen. sg., Ionic -ης (= Attic -ας)
ἀτρεΐδαο: Ἀτρεΐδης — son of Atreus, i.e. Agamemnon; gen. sg., epic (-αο = Attic -ου) · also son of Atreus, i.e. Menelaus; masc. gen. sg.
ἀτρεΐδη: Ἀτρεΐδης — son of Atreus; masc. voc. sg.
ἀχαιοί: Ἀχαιοί — the Achaeans, the Greeks; masc. nom. pl.
ἀχαιῶν: Ἀχαιοί — the Achaeans, the Greeks; gen. pl.
ἀχιλλεύς: Ἀχιλλεύς — Achilles, son of Peleus, chief Greek hero at Troy; masc. nom. sg.
ἀχιλλεὺς: Ἀχιλλεύς — Achilles, son of Peleus; masc. nom. sg.
ἀχιλῆος: Ἀχιλλεύς — Achilles; masc. gen. sg., single-λ epic (= Attic Ἀχιλλέως)
ἀχιλῆϊ: Ἀχιλλεύς — Achilles; masc. dat. sg., single-λ epic (= Attic Ἀχιλλεῖ)
ἁπάντων: ἅπας — all, the whole of; masc. gen. pl., of comparison after προβέβηκας: ’beyond all’ · also partitive gen. after a superlative: ’of all’ (νεώτατος ἁπάντων ’youngest of all’)
ἂν: ἀνά — up, aboard; prep./preverb, with apocope ἂν before δ’; in tmesis (ἂν … βήσομεν ’put aboard’) · also modal particle ἄν (= κεν) written ἂν: with the opt., potential: ’would’; with the subj. after εὖτ’: ’whenever’ · also with ὡς + subj.: ’in the way that’ (ὡς ἂν ἐγὼ εἴπω ’as I may say’) · also modal particle with the subj. after ὅτ’: ’whenever’ (ὅτ’ ἂν … γένωνται ’whenever they come to be’) · also modal particle with a fut. or short-vowel subj.: ’could’ (οὐκ ἂν … μυθήσομαι ’I could not tell’) · also εἴ περ ἂν + opt., ’even if … should’ · also εἴ περ ἂν + subj., ’even if … ever’ (εἴ περ ἂν αὐτὸν σεύωνται ’even if they set upon him’) · also εἰ … ἂν + subj., ’if ever, should’ (εἰ δ’ ἂν … ἐθέλωσιν ’but if they should be unwilling’) · also with an indic. past tense, contrary to fact: ’would have’ (ἂν … ἦεν ’would have been’) · also modal particle ἄν with the subj. after ὄφρα: ’until, while’ (ὄφρ’ ἂν … βείω ’until I go’) · also modal particle ἄν after ἐπεί + subj.: ’once’ (ἐπεὶ ἂν … ἐπίσπῃς ’once you have met’) · also modal particle with the subj. in a general relative clause: ’whomever’ (ὃν … ἂν … νοήσω ’whomever I notice’)
ἃς: ὅς, ἥ, ὅ — who, which; relative pron., fem. acc. pl.: ’which’
ἄγε: ἄγε — come now!; interjectional imper. of ἄγω, 2 sg. · also ἄγω — lead; impf. 3 sg., unaugmented (= ἦγε): ’led’ · also ἄγω — lead; pres. imper. 2 sg.: ’lead’ (μή μ’ ἄγε κεῖσ’ ’do not lead me there’)
ἄειδε: ἀείδω — sing; pres. imper. 2 sg. · also impf. 3 sg., unaugmented
ἄνακτι: ἄναξ — lord, king, master; masc. dat. sg.
ἄναξ: ἄναξ — lord, master; masc. nom. sg. · also voc. sg. (same form), in address: ’lord!’ (κλῦθι, ἄναξ ’hear me, lord’)
ἄποινα: ἄποινα — ransom (a neuter plural noun); nom./acc. pl.
ἄρα: ἄρα — so, then, as it turned out; inferential particle
ἄργος: Ἄργος — Argos, the Argive land (Greece); neut. nom./acc. sg. · also the Pelasgian Argos, a district of northern Greece; neut. acc. sg.
ἄστυ: ἄστυ — town, city; neut. acc. sg.
ἅλις: ἅλις — in crowds, in abundance, enough; adv.
ἅμ: ἅμα (elided ἅμ’) — together with, at the same time, along; adv./prep. + dat.
ἐγγὺς: ἐγγύς — near, close by; adv. · also prep. + gen.: ’near’
ἐθέλω: ἐθέλω — wish, be willing; pres. 1 sg.
ἐθέλῃσι: ἐθέλω — wish, be willing; pres. subj. 3 sg. act., epic -σι (= Attic ἐθέλῃ), after αἴ κ’: ’if he wishes’
ἐκ: ἐκ (ἐξ before a vowel) — out of, from; + gen. · also as adverb or preverb in tmesis, no case expressed: ’out’ (ἐκ δ’ ἔβαν ’and out they stepped’)
ἐλεήσῃ: ἐλεέω — pity, have mercy; aor. subj. 3 sg., in a condition after αἴ κε: ’if she take pity’
ἐμὰς: ἐμός — my, mine; fem. acc. pl.
ἐμῷ: ἐμός — my, mine; masc. dat. sg.
ἐν: ἐν — in, on, among; + dat.; also used as an adverb, ’in it, there’ · also as preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (ἐν … βάλῃ = ἐμβάλῃ ’cast in’; ἐν … χεῦον = ἔγχεον ’pour in’)
ἐνάρων: ἔναρα — spoils stripped from the slain (neut. pl. only); neut. gen. pl.
ἐνὶ: ἐν (epic ἐνί) — in, on, among; + dat. · also adverb or preverb, no case: ’therein’ (ἔνθ’ ἐνὶ πέπλοι ... βεβλήατο ’therein coverlets were laid’) · also + gen., of a person’s house: ’in the house of’ (ἐνὶ Κίρκης ’in Circe’s house’)
ἐξ: ἐκ (ἐξ before a vowel) — out of, from; + gen. · also as a preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (ἐξ … ἕντο = ἐξέντο, from ἐξίημι ’send out, put away (desire)’)
ἐπέτελλε: ἐπιτέλλω — lay charge on, enjoin (+ dat. + inf.); impf. 3 sg.: ’laid charge’
ἐπί: ἐπί — on, upon, towards; prep. + dat./acc./gen., accented before the enclitic τε; ἐπί τε … καί ’both to … and’ · also preverb in tmesis (ἐπί τ’ … ἠμύει ’bows down upon’)
ἐπαρξάμενοι: ἐπάρχομαι — begin a rite, pour the first drops of a libation; aor. part. mid. masc. nom. pl.: ’having made the first pouring’
ἐπεστέψαντο: ἐπιστέφω — crown, fill to the brim (from στέφω); aor. 3 pl. mid.
ἐπὶ: ἐπί — on, upon, to, against; + dat./acc./gen.; also a preverb in tmesis (ἐπὶ … ἔτελλε = ἐπέτελλε) · also + dat., ’in aid of, on behalf of’ (ἐπὶ Τρώεσσιν ἀρῆξαι ’to help the Trojans’) · also + acc. of duration, ’for’ (ἐπὶ χρόνον ’for a time’) · also + acc. of extent, ’over, along’ (ἐπὶ νῶτον ’along the back’) · also + acc. of the thing aimed at, ’for’ (ἐπὶ τεύχεα ’for the armour’) · also + gen., ’toward’ (μελαινάων ἐπὶ νηῶν ’toward the black ships’) · also + gen. of time, ’in the time of’ (ἐπὶ προτέρων ἀνθρώπων ’in the time of earlier men’) · also adv., ’next, after’ (ἐπὶ δὲ πλήξιππον Ὀρέστην ’and next Orestes’)
ἐς: εἰς (epic ἐς) — into, to; + acc. · also as a preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb with no case expressed (ἐς … ἦλθον = εἰσῆλθον ’came in’)
ἐϋκτιμένην: ἐΰκτίμενος — well-built, well-founded; fem. acc. sg., epic ἐϋ- (= εὖ); said of a town
ἐόντα: εἰμί — be; pres. part., epic (= Attic ὄντα); masc. acc. sg. · also neut. nom./acc. pl.: τά τ’ ἐόντα ’the things that are’
ἑ: ἕ — him, her, it; epic encl. acc. sg. reflexive/personal pron. (= Attic αὐτόν/-ήν/-ό)
ἑκάστῳ: ἕκαστος — each, every; masc. dat. sg.
ἑλένην: Ἑλένη — Helen, wife of Menelaus; fem. acc. sg.
ἔειπεν: εἶπον — say, speak; aor. 3 sg., epic augmented (ἔ-ειπεν, = Attic εἶπεν)
ἔνθα: ἔνθα — there, then; adverb of place or time · also relative, ’where’ (ἔνθα πάρος κοιμᾶθ’ ’where he used to sleep’) · also ἔνθα καὶ ἔνθα ’hither and thither, this way and that’
ἔνι: ἐν — in; prep. + dat., postpositive with accent thrown back after its noun (νέεσσ’ ἔνι = Attic ἐν ναυσί)
ἔπειτ: ἔπειτα (elided ἔπειτ’) — then, next, after that
ἔπειτα: ἔπειτα — then, next, after that; adv.
ἔργα: ἔργον — deed, work; neut. nom./acc. pl. · also ’tilled land, farmland’ (ἔργα νέμοντο ’inhabited the farmlands’)
ἔσσεται: εἰμί — be; fut. 3 sg., epic doubled σ (= Attic ἔσται)
ἔχευαν: χέω — pour; aor. 3 pl. act., epic -αν (= Attic ἔχεαν) · also with σύν in tmesis: σὺν … ἔχευαν ’poured together, confounded’ (of oaths)
ἔχθιστος: ἔχθιστος — most hateful; superl. of ἐχθρός, masc. nom. sg.
ἕδος: ἕδος — seat, abode; neut. nom./acc. sg.
ἕκαστον: ἕκαστος — each, every; masc. acc. sg.: ’each (man)’
ἕλεν: αἱρέω — take, seize; in battle, kill; aor. 2 3 sg., unaugmented, ν-movable (= Attic εἷλεν)
ἕπτ: ἑπτά — seven; indeclinable numeral, elided (ἕπτ’ = ἑπτά)
ἠδὲ: ἠδέ — and; epic conj. (τε … ἠδέ ’both … and’)
ἠετίωνος: Ἠετίων — Eëtion, king of Thebe, father of Andromache; masc. gen. sg.
ἠμαθόεντος: ἠμαθόεις — sandy (epithet of Pylos); masc. gen. sg.
ἠμείβετ: ἀμείβω — exchange; mid. answer, reply; impf. 3 sg. mid., elided (ἠμείβετ’ = ἠμείβετο)
ἡγεῖτο: ἡγέομαι — lead, go first (+ gen.); impf. 3 sg. mid.: ’was leading’
ἣ: ὅς, ἥ, ὅ — who, which; relative pron., fem. nom. sg. (grave, mid-clause form) · also demonstrative, ’she’ (ἣ δ’ … βεβήκει) · also demonstrative in the correlative ἣ μὲν … ἣ δέ: ’one … another’
ἣν: ὅς, ἥ, ὅν (possessive) — his own, her own; fem. acc. sg. · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅν: whom, which (fem. acc. sg.)
ἥν: ὅς, ἥ, ὅ — who, which; relative pron., fem. acc. sg.: ’whom’; not the possessive · also possessive ὅς, ἥ, ὅν — her own; fem. acc. sg., agreeing with a noun: ’her own’ (θυγατέρα ἥν ’her own daughter’)
ἦ: ἦ — truly, surely; affirming particle; ἦ μέν in oaths · also an interrogative particle · also ἠμί — say; impf. 3 sg. ἦ ’he said’, in ἦ καί, ἦ ῥα · also ἦ = ἤ, ’or’ (εἰ … ἦ ’whether … or’)
ἦεν: εἰμί — be; impf. 3 sg., epic ἦεν (= Attic ἦν)
ἱκέσθην: ἱκνέομαι — come to, reach; aor. 3 dual (strong aor., ἱκέσθην), + acc. of goal: ’the two came to’
ἱππότα: ἱππότα — horseman, charioteer (epithet of Nestor); masc. nom. sg., old form in short -α (= ἱππότης)
ἱρὴν: ἱερός (epic ἱρός) — holy, sacred; fem. acc. sg., epic ἱρήν (= Attic ἱεράν)
ἴδε: ὁράω — see; aor. 3 sg., unaugmented, from the root of εἶδον (= εἶδε): ’saw’
ἶσον: ἴσος — equal, like; neut. acc. sg.: ’equal’, or adverbial ’equally’ · also masc. acc. sg., + dat.: ’equal (to)’ (ὃν ἶσον ἐτίομεν ’whom we honoured as equal’)
ὀδίος: Ὀδίος — Odius, a leader of the Halizones; masc. nom. sg.
ὀδυσσεύς: Ὀδυσσεύς — Odysseus, king of Ithaca; masc. nom. sg.
ὀδυσσῆϊ: Ὀδυσσεύς — Odysseus; masc. dat. sg., epic -ῆϊ (= Attic Ὀδυσσεῖ)
ὀμοῦμαι: ὄμνυμι — swear; fut. 1 sg. mid. (contracted from ὀμόσσομαι): ’I shall swear’
ὀνομήνω: ὀνομαίνω — name, call by name; aor. subj. 1 sg. (fut. has the same form), potential with ἂν: ’I could name’
ὁπότε: ὁπότε — whenever, when; temporal conj., + opt. in a general clause
ὄφρα: ὄφρα — so that, in order that (+ subj.) · also temporal, ’until, while’ · also + opt. in a purpose clause after a past tense: ’so that … might’ (ὄφρα νέμοιτο ’so that he might enjoy’) · also + fut. indic. in a purpose clause: ’so that … will’ (ὄφρα … εἴσεται ’so that … will know’)
ὅ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it (in Homer a pronoun); masc. nom. sg., with γε ’he’ · also relative neut. ’which’; ὅ τι ’whatever, why’ · also neut. acc. sg. as a conjunction after a verb of seeing: ’that’ · also neut. acc. sg. as a conjunction after a verb of emotion: ’that, because’ (χωόμενος ὅ τ’ … ’angry that …’) · also neut. acc. sg. as a conjunction after a verb of knowing: ’that’ (ὅ τ’ ἄριστον … οὐδὲν ἔτισεν) · also εἰς ὅ (κεν) + subj., ’until’ (εἰς ὅ κεν … ἕλωμεν ’until we take’) · also masc. nom. sg. ’he’ without γε (ὅ σφιν ’he … to them’) · also relative ὅς, masc. nom. sg., ’who’ (ὅ με … κάκ’ ἔοργε ’who did me wrong’)
ὅν: ὅς, ἥ, ὅ — who, which; relative pron., masc. acc. sg.: ’whom’
ὅς: ὅς, ἥ, ὅ (relative) — who, which; masc. nom. sg., accented before an enclitic · also ὅς τις as an indirect interrogative: ’who’ (ὅς τις ὅδ’ ἐστίν ’who this is’)
ὅσον: ὅσος — as much as, as many as, as far as; neut. acc. sg., adverbial: ’as far as’
ὅσσ: ὅσος (epic ὅσσος, double σ) — as much/many as; neut. acc. pl., elided (ὅσσ’ = ὅσσα): ’as many as’
ὅσσά: ὅσος — as great, as many as; neut. nom. pl., epic -σσ- (= Attic ὅσα): ’as many as’ · also neut. acc. pl., object of its verb: ’whatever’ (ὅσσά κεν αὐτοὶ δῶσιν ’whatever they themselves may give’)
ὅσσον: ὅσος (epic ὅσσος) — as much/great as; neut. acc. sg. used adverbially: ’how much, how far’
ὑμῖν: σύ (pl. ὑμεῖς) — you; dat. pl.: ’to you’
ὑπὸ: ὑπό — under, beneath; adv. and preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (ὑπὸ … τάνυσσαν ’stretched under’) · also prep. + acc. of motion: ’to, under’ (ὑπὸ Ἴλιον ἦλθον ’came to Ilios’) · also prep. + dat., ’under, beneath’ (ὑπὸ πλατανίστῳ ’beneath a plane-tree’) · also prep. + dat. with τίκτω, of the father: ’to’ (ὑπὸ Πειριθόῳ τέκετο ’bore to Peirithous’) · also prep. + gen.: ’beneath, from under’ (ὑπὸ στέρνοιο ’beneath the breast’) · also prep. + gen. of cause: ’under (the blast of)’ (ὑπὸ Ζεφύροιο ἰωῆς) · also prep. + dat. of cause, placed after its noun: ’under the weight of’ (καμάτῳ … ὑπό ’from toil’)
ὠκὺς: ὠκύς — swift; masc. nom. sg.; πόδας ὠκύς ’swift in feet’
ὡς: ὡς — as, how, that; conj. (unaccented) introducing a fact: ’that’ · also causal: ’since, seeing that’ · also temporal, ’when’ (ὡς ἴδον ’when they saw’) · also final, ’so that’ (+ subj./opt.): ὡς φρήτρη … ἀρήγῃ ’so that clan may help clan’ · also introducing a wish, with ὄφελεν: ’would that’ (ὡς ὄφελεν θάνατός μοι ἁδεῖν ’would that death had pleased me’) · also in a comparison, ’like, just as’ (ὡς ὅδε οἶνος ’like this wine’) · also ὡς εἴ, ’as if’ (ὡς εἴ τι κακὸν ῥέζουσαν ’as if doing some evil’)
ὣς: ὥς — thus, so; adverb (accented, distinct from unaccented ὡς ’as’; = Attic οὕτως); ὣς ἔφατ’ ’so he spoke’ · also ὣς = ὡς, ’like, as’ after its noun (κακὸν ὣς ’like a coward’)
ᾧ: ὅς, ἥ, ὅ — who, which; relative, masc./neut. dat. sg.: ’to whom’ · also possessive, ’his own’
ῥηϊδίως: ῥηΐδιος — easy; adv. ῥηϊδίως: ’easily, readily’, epic (= Attic ῥᾳδίως)
